div.head: Northu 52
div.ab: Gif landagende man ætsace, þonne nemne man him his gelican ealswa micel wente swa cyninges þegne; gif him þæt berste, gilde lahsliht: VI healfmarc.
Gif landagende man ætsace, þonne nemne man him his gelican ealswa micel wente swa cyninges þegne; gif him þæt berste, gilde lahsliht: VI healfmarc.

Wenn ein Mann mit Landeigen [ohne Hofdienstadel das] leugnen will, dann ernenne man [das Gericht] ihm von seinen Standesgenossen ebenso grosse Eideshilfe[?] wie dem Königsthegn; wenn ihm das misslingt, zahle er Rechtsbruchbusse: 6 Halbmark.

If a land-owning man [without court-service nobility] wishes to deny [it], then let [the court] nominate for him from his equals as large a body of oath-helpers[?] as for a king's thegn; if that fails him, let him pay lahslit: 6 half-marks.
If a landowner denies it, then as many compurgators, his equals, are to be nominated for him as for a king’s thegn; if that fails, he is to pay lahslit: 6 half-marks.
If a landholder denies the charge, then just as many witnesses of his same status are to be chosen for him as for a king’s thane; if that fails, he is to pay lahslit: six half-marks.
div.note: Thorpe corrects ‘gelican’ to ‘gelicena’ as in 53; but compare Sievers, Grammar 304.2. ‘wente’ is corrupt, Liebermann thinks, from Norse ‘vitni’ (a collective neuter singular, Heusler).; U: checked against Whitelock, EHD I (1979), and corrected (before: ‘If a landowner denies it, then as many compurgators, his equals, are to be nominated for him as for a king's thegn; if that fails, he is then to pay lahslit: 6 half-marks.’).; W: corrected against Rabin p. 311, October 2026 (was “If a landholder denies the charge, then just as many witnesses of his same status are to be chosen for him as for a king’s thane; if that fails, he is to pay lahslit: six half-marks.”, now “If a landholder denies the charge, then just as many witnesses of his same status are to be chosen for him as for a king’s thane; if that fails, he is to pay lahslit: six half-marks. (expanded letters in italics: lahslit)”)

Frühere sahen in wente dasselbe wie wallerwente o. 51³. Dagegen spricht, dass jene hier durchs Gericht ernannt, diese dort vom Hauptschwörer hinzugenommen werden. Vermutlich ist in 52. 53 hinzuzudenken eine Zahl von 24 Eideshelfern, halb aus Verwandten, halb aus Unverwandten

Earlier scholars saw in wente the same thing as wallerwente above 51³. Against this is the fact that the former are here nominated by the court, whereas the latter are there added by the principal swearer. Presumably a number of 24 oath-helpers is to be understood in 52. 53, half of them kinsmen and half non-kinsmen
